note: Each SVG has a light file and a -dark file: use the dark one when the site theme is dark.

illustrations.name: pipeline
illustrations.heading: How one frame is made
illustrations.alt: Five steps from top to bottom: your project (TSX or an HTML page), Node runs it for each frame with the React reconciler or the HyperFrames runtime, the result is scene JSON, a Rust GPU compositor in an N-API addon draws it, and FFmpeg encodes the video. A dashed outline marks the whole path as having no browser.

illustrations.name: pure-frame
illustrations.heading: Rules the engine keeps
illustrations.alt: The project and a frame number go into the renderer, and a picture comes out. Rendering the same project and frame again, on another worker or out of order, gives the identical picture. The wall clock is not an input.

illustrations.name: render-paths
illustrations.heading: Where they differ
illustrations.alt: Three rows. Remotion: you write TSX and React, a browser draws every frame, you get a video. HyperFrames: you write an HTML page with GSAP, a browser draws every frame, you get a video. Kinetograph: you write TSX or an HTML page, a Rust compositor draws every frame on the GPU, you get a video, with no browser.

illustrations.name: project-structure
illustrations.heading: A TSX project
illustrations.alt: A project folder with src for your code (index.tsx, scenes/Title.tsx, components, lib), public for images, fonts, audio and video, and out for everything the commands write: stills, sheets and renders. package.json, tsconfig.json and .gitignore sit beside them.

illustrations.name: studio-loop
illustrations.heading: Mark up the preview
illustrations.alt: A loop of four steps. One: the preview shows frames drawn by the engine. Two: you mark up a frame or a span of time. Three: your coding agent edits the code. Four: the engine redraws the frame, which goes back to the preview.

illustrations.name: sequences
illustrations.heading: Sequence, Series, Loop and Freeze
illustrations.alt: A timeline of 120 frames. A Sequence from frame 30 for 60 frames sits on it, and a nested Sequence with from 20 and 30 frames sits inside the first. Frame 50 of the composition is frame 20 inside the first Sequence and frame 0 inside the nested one, because each Sequence counts from its own start.

illustrations.name: effects-chain
illustrations.heading: Order
illustrations.alt: A layer’s pixels go through its effects in array order, first colorCorrection and then lut. Then the layer is cut by clip, mask and matte, then opacity and blendMode apply, and it is composited with the layers below.

illustrations.name: video-matting
illustrations.heading: Recipes
illustrations.alt: A video goes through a model that runs once before rendering. It writes a foreground, the subject with alpha, and a base, the original picture. Layered back to front, the base, then text, then the foreground, give a result with the text behind the subject.
illustrations.also: the page is on the feat/video-matting-api branch

illustrations.name: render-options
illustrations.heading: Look at frames
illustrations.alt: A grid of commands against four stages: bundle, run, draw and encode. doctor stops after run and never uses the GPU. still, strip and onion go through draw for a chosen frame, frames or range. render with sequence stops after draw and writes an image per frame. render goes through all four to an MP4.

videos.name: pipeline
videos.heading: How one frame is made
videos.alt: Looping animation of two frames travelling from your project through Node, scene JSON and the Rust GPU compositor to FFmpeg and a video file. A header and a dashed outline mark the whole path as having no browser.

videos.name: pure-frame
videos.heading: Rules the engine keeps
videos.alt: Looping animation of a project and a frame number going into a pure render function. The number changes from 12 to 24 and the picture changes with it. When 12 comes back, the picture equals the earlier one for frame 12. No wall clock is used.

videos.name: studio-loop
videos.heading: Mark up the preview
videos.alt: Looping animation of Studio's four steps in turn: the preview, you mark up a frame with a box and a note, your coding agent edits a line of code, and the engine redraws the frame.
